messages:
Maya (Product): Quick sync — we need to lock the v2 route deprecation timeline and exactly what compatibility guarantees we promise for paying customers.
Dmitri (Eng): +1. Key tradeoffs: 1) keep v1 runtime for N months, 2) provide compatibility shim that rewrites calls, or 3) forcing migration with automated conversion tools. Each has perf/cost implications.
Eva (CS): Customers keep asking for a clear cutoff date. Enterprise customers want at least 6 months notice and a migration checklist.
Ashley (Platform): From infra POV, maintaining v1 runtime doubles testing surface. Shim option looks attractive if it can be kept stateless and light.
Kevin (SRE): Important: fallback behavior when v2 is overloaded. If we accept v1 calls on v2 infra via shim, we need traffic shaping and circuit-breakers. That adds SLO risk.
Maya (Product): Draft proposal: 3-month overlap with a compatibility shim that handles the most common v1 patterns (chat/completions, embeddings). We offer per-customer migration plans for enterprise accounts.
Dmitri (Eng): Technical constraints: function-calling and structured output semantics changed in v2. Shim can translate simple tool-call shapes but not all edge cases. Suggest: shim covers 80% telemetry-driven patterns and returns a clear 409 with migration hints when unsupported.
Sam (Legal): Make sure deprecation notices and data retention language align with contracts. Any forced behavior that modifies payloads needs opt-in for customers with compliance needs.
Eva (CS): We should publish a migration guide + automated lint tool that flags incompatible patterns in prompts and code. That reduces support load.
Ashley (Platform): Proposed rollout plan:
- Week 0: announce deprecation and migration docs
- Week 4: enable opt-in shim (beta) for customers
- Week 8: enable shim globally in compatibility mode with verbose logs
- Week 12: start rejecting unsupported v1 calls (409 + migration-url)
- Week 16: remove v1 endpoints entirely for hosted API
Kevin (SRE): Ops checklist: monitor error spikes, token-cost delta, shim CPU/mem, canary in 2 regions, rollback knob.
Maya (Product): Launch criteria:
- Migration docs and examples published
- Lint tool v0.1 available and tested on 5 enterprise customers
- Shim covers top-5 incompat patterns and has <1% latency p50 overhead in staging
- Legal sign-off on notice language
Dmitri (Eng): We need to enumerate top incompat patterns. From telemetry: 1) new function calling schema, 2) response-format markers for structured output, 3) embedding dimension changes, 4) header routing differences, 5) model-name mapping.
Maya (Product): Action items:
- @Dmitri: doc 80% shim translation matrix + failure modes (due EOD Tue)
- @Ashley: infra cost estimate for running shim in production (due Thu)
- @Eva: draft migration checklist and onboarding email templates (due Wed)
- @Kevin: ops rollback playbook and metrics dashboard fields (due Fri)
- @Sam: finalize contract/notice language (due Thu)
deploy-bot: deploy triggered for branch "v2-compat-shim/prototype" to staging at 2048500300
Dmitri (Eng): prototype deployed. Quick perf note: shim adds ~12ms p50 on small requests, ~40ms on long-completions due to parsing. Working on micro-optimizations.
Eva (CS): Can we add a migration-tag header so we can selectively route long-running migrations off critical infra? Customer requests it.
Ashley (Platform): Yes, we can support X-Redwood-Migrate header. Will add routing rule to prefer dedicated pool for headers with that tag.
Maya (Product): One open negotiation: enterprise customers asking for "extended overlap" (9-12 months) in contracts. Tradeoff: operational burden vs revenue/retention. We should surface cost-to-serve per month to sales.
Kevin (SRE): If we agree to extended overlap, we need a cost-recovery surcharge or a special reserved pool. Otherwise ops will be constantly firefighting.
Maya (Product): OK — next step: compile cost and risk numbers, then present to GTM for special contract templates. We'll reconvene next Tue. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
